transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Liam, Priya (Redwood) / Carlos, Aisha, Noah, Riley (Sandspring)
Agenda: Sprint 4 bench readout, tune notes, decide next head-to-head tests, security handoff

[00:00:06] Maya: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda recap - we want to run through the sprint 4 results, highlight the latency/throughput deltas versus the incumbent, and agree on follow-ups.
[00:00:18] Carlos: yep, thanks. we got the last run results from your team yesterday, skimmed them. Aisha has a few questions on the quantize setup.
[00:00:27] Aisha: yeah so, first up - when you say "tuned quant" are you doing dynamic quant or static 4-bit? I think the report said q4_k or something but text was a bit off.
[00:00:36] Liam: right so it's basically q4_k per-layer profile, we ran two variants: q4_k static and a mixed mode where attention kernels stay fp16 for tail accuracy. the file label in the report got mangled - appears as "q4k_opt" in some rows, sorry about transcription.
[00:00:49] Riley: (soft) okay.
[00:00:51] [00:00:52] Priya: quick context - baseline IncumbentX numbers were their managed endpoint with auto-scaling. they reported p50 85ms, p90 210ms for the 1k token workload. Redwood's early runs were promising, but we need throughput numbers at concurrency 40.
[00:01:08] Maya: yep. so headline: on the canonical 1k token prompt set, Redwood (quant tuned, KV prefix caching on) hit p50 ~63ms, p90 ~150ms and p99 around 420ms under representative traffic at 40 concurrency. throughput sustained at 220 RPS with batching target of 8. IncumbentX matched about 140 RPS under the same concurrency and had a heavier tail at p99 ~600ms.
[00:01:34] Carlos: that's helpful. those are medians and p90s i saw too. but we noticed during the burst window (sudden 2x traffic for ~90s) your p99 spiked to 1.1s on one run, which worries us.
[00:01:46] Liam: correct, that's where we had an artifact in the routing - some requests landed on warm-but-not-hot workers and the KV cache miss forced KV recompute which increases latency. we have a mitigation: a tiny warmup policy to keep a hot pool for prefix reuse and also adaptive batching priority to prefer low-latency slots.
[00:02:02] Aisha: can you explain the KV thing simply? i may be missing an infra detail.
[00:02:06] Liam: sure - KV cache here is the transformer key/value cache for long context reuse. when you reuse prefixes we avoid recomputing attention states. but if a request hits a new instance without populated KV, the system has to replay some parts which adds ~300-600ms depending on sequence length.
[00:02:22] [00:02:25] Noah: that sounds like a placement problem on our side too, because our test harness spins up stress containers and sometimes tears them down between bursts. is there a way to pin workers for the dedicated slot?
[00:02:35] Maya: yes for dedicated slots we provide pinned GPU pools, that eliminates warm start misses. Liam, can you note the dedicated-slot ask?
[00:02:42] Liam: noted - we'll schedule a short-lived dedicated slot for an 8-hour controlled head-to-head so we can remove placement variance.
[00:02:49] Carlos: and the quality delta with q4_k - did you run nll or human evals? because for our clinical summarization even small hallucination rates are bad.
[00:02:58] Liam: we ran automated BLEU-ish and ROUGE proxies and spot human checks on 300 prompts. mixed-mode kept regression within noise (<0.8% metric delta). we flagged a few cases where numeric fidelity dropped; we can blacklist prompt patterns or keep fp16 for those calls.
[00:03:14] Aisha: can you add those example prompts to the report? we need to see them.
[00:03:17] Priya: will do - Aisha we'll paste the suspicious cases into the shared sheet.
[00:03:21] [00:03:25] Maya: walking through the results doc: page 2 shows latency histogram, page 3 has throughput vs concurrency. note we tested batching at 4/8/16 - optimal was 8 for latency/throughput tradeoff. at 16 latency p50 increased but throughput marginally higher.
[00:03:43] Carlos: what about cost? your per-token numbers look lower but with dedicated slot reservation how does that net out?
[00:03:49] Maya: good question. the model-level per-token compute is about 25% cheaper than IncumbentX on host pricing due to quant and kernel optimizations; but if you reserve a 24/7 dedicated pool the fixed cost shifts the breakeven point. our cost model spreadsheet (link in chat) shows break-even at ~120k tokens/day for dedicated. until then hosted with burst capacity is more efficient.
[00:04:09] Noah: can you send that spreadsheet again? the link we have 404'd.
[00:04:12] Maya: sure i'll re-share after the call.
[00:04:14] [00:04:18] Aisha: on the routing playbook - do you support percent-based canary (like 5% traffic to Redwood, 95% incumbent) with automatic fallback?
[00:04:24] Liam: yes - we have routing policies by percent and latency headroom. we can route a fraction and auto-failover to incumbent if p95 exceeds a threshold for x minutes. we tested failover during the last sprint in a lab.
[00:04:36] Carlos: nice. during failover do you preserve in-flight requests?
[00:04:39] Liam: in-flight can't be moved mid-token; but our fallback is at request granularity so new requests will go to fallback. we also have a grace policy to let existing streams finish.
[00:04:48] [00:04:50] Riley: quick interjection - security: we need SOC2 type II, SAML SSO, and KMS integration. where are we on that?
[00:04:57] Priya: we flagged that last week - maya can you point them to the security packet.
[00:05:01] Maya: yes, we have SOC2 docs and an HSM/KMS integration guide. i'll include the SOC2 report redacted copy and our KMS design note. can you confirm who the central reviewer is?
[00:05:11] Carlos: that's me. i'll review for compliance and get back with any follow-ups.
[00:05:14] [00:05:20] Aisha: returning to the weird p99 spike - you mentioned a warm pool mitigation. how many hot workers do you suggest for our profile?
[00:05:26] Liam: for the 250 RPS 1k token distribution we suggest keeping ~6-8 hot workers with prefix cache pinned, plus elastic warmers. for dedicated slot we can pin 10 to be conservative.
[00:05:37] Noah: that'll cost more. can we do an autoscaler that keeps min 6 during day and 2 at night?
[00:05:42] Maya: yes, autoscaling policies are configurable. we'll show a sample policy in the routing playbook.
[00:05:46] [00:05:50] Carlos: one more question - egress and residency. our data residency needs mean we can't let inference logs leave region. can Redwood run in our VPC or on-prem?
[00:05:58] Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages. we can run the inference nodes in your VPC and keep logs in your KMS/region. i'll connect you to the private deploy folks after this sprint.
[00:06:09] Priya: note: checklist item for SOC2 handoff to private team.
[00:06:13] [00:06:20] Carlos: okay let's align on the next test cadence - we want an 8-hour dedicated head-to-head to remove placement variance and then a 24h sustained at 250RPS to validate cost and p99 under realistic churn.
[00:06:29] Maya: agreed. we'll provision the dedicated slot for the 8hr run next week, and you'll run the 24h sustained after we share the tuned profile.
[00:06:36] Aisha: can we also capture probabilistic error reproduction for those hallucination cases? i.e. rerun the 12 flagged prompts under both configs.
[00:06:42] Liam: yes we'll run the A/B prompts with identical seeds and config.
[00:06:45] [00:06:50] Maya: to recap quick: 1) Redwood sends tuned quant profile + cost model (Maya) 2) Redwood provisions 8hr dedicated slot (Liam) 3) Sandspring runs 24h sustained load and posts logs (Carlos/Noah) 4) Security packet and SOC2 docs shared (Maya), Carlos to confirm reviewer.
[00:07:08] Carlos: perfect. anything else on the bench numbers?
[00:07:11] Aisha: i'd like the run-level CSVs for each trial so we can graph ourselves, sometimes the aggregated numbers hide weird tails.
[00:07:18] Maya: we'll drop the CSVs in the folder.
[00:07:20] [00:07:25] Riley: small note - competitor call next week with BigCloudAI, might influence timing but we want this head-to-head regardless.
[00:07:32] Priya: ok noted.
[00:07:35] [00:07:40] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow-up in email with the provisioning window and the spreadsheet link. next sync same time next week unless we need a quick mid-week check after the dedicated run.
[00:07:50] Carlos: thanks all, bye.
[00:07:53] Aisha: bye.

(Transcript clipped - meeting ran ~48 minutes; additional technical back-and-forth on kernel selection and microbench stacks continued in private channel.)
